prompt: What does an organisation need, and a person does not, to enrol in either store?

choices.text: A Mac
choices.why: Neither kind of account needs a Mac to enrol.

choices.text: A published app on the other store first
choices.why: Neither store asks for that.

choices.text: A D-U-N-S number
choices.why: Right. It identifies the company and can take days to obtain.

choices.text: A bank in the United States
choices.why: Banks in many countries are accepted.

prompt: Ana publishes the planner from a personal Apple account. What does every listing show as the seller?

choices.text: Her full legal name
choices.why: Right. The seller name of a personal account is the person's.

choices.text: The app's name, Study Planner
choices.why: The app's name is separate from the seller's.

choices.text: Any nickname she enters at enrolment
choices.why: The seller name comes from the verified identity.

choices.text: Nothing until the app earns money
choices.why: It is shown from the first day the app is live.

prompt: A two-person studio expects to sell the planner to a company in a year. Which account should it open now, and why?

choices.text: A personal one, since a transfer later is instant
choices.why: Transfers are possible but slow, with agreements and tax on both sides.

choices.text: Two personal ones, one per founder, to split the risk
choices.why: That splits the app's history and its users across two sellers.

choices.text: None until the sale, to avoid the fees
choices.why: Without an account there is no app to sell.

choices.text: An organisation
choices.why: Right. The account then outlives either founder and carries the company's name.

prompt: Apple publishes a new developer agreement and uploads stop. Who can make them start again?

choices.text: Any Admin of the team
choices.why: Admins manage users and apps, but cannot sign agreements.

choices.text: Only the team's Account Holder
choices.why: Right. Only that person signs Apple's agreements.

choices.text: The developer who uploaded the last build
choices.why: Uploading gives no power over agreements.

choices.text: Apple, after thirty days
choices.why: Nothing restarts on its own; the agreement has to be accepted.

prompt: Match each person to the least App Store Connect role that does their job.
A tester coordinator should release builds to closed testing and never to production. Where can that line be drawn exactly?

choices.text: In App Store Connect, with the Developer role
choices.why: Apple's fixed roles do not separate testing from release that finely.

choices.text: In Play Console permissions
choices.why: Right. Releasing to testing tracks and to production are separate permissions.

choices.text: Nowhere: both stores make releasing all or nothing
choices.why: Google's permissions separate them.

choices.text: By sharing the owner's login only on test days
choices.why: A shared login cannot say who released anything.

prompt: Which of these are rules the lesson gives for keeping an account safe? Choose every one.

choices.text: One person, one login
choices.why: Right. Otherwise nobody can say who pressed release.

choices.text: Remove a contractor's access on their last day
choices.why: Right. Access ends when the work ends.

choices.text: Make every developer an Admin so nobody is blocked
choices.why: That is the default the rules exist to avoid.

choices.text: Two-factor authentication on every account that can release
choices.why: Right.

prompt: A one-off in-app purchase costs 9.99. Under Apple's Small Business Program, and ignoring tax, how much reaches the developer, in dollars?
Why does `proceeds.ts` count in whole cents instead of dollars with decimals?

choices.text: Node cannot print decimals
choices.why: It can; `toFixed(2)` does at the end.

choices.text: The stores forbid decimals in prices
choices.why: Prices have decimals; the issue is arithmetic.

choices.text: Cents make the script faster
choices.why: Speed is not the reason; exactness is.

choices.text: Floating point cannot hold amounts like 0.1 exactly, and sums drift
choices.why: Right. Integers of cents add up exactly.

prompt: The planner adds a paid feature that books a one-to-one tutoring session over video, held outside the app. What commission does the store take on it?

choices.text: None, as for a taxi ride
choices.why: Right. A service used outside the app is not a digital good the store sells.

choices.text: The usual 15% or 30%, since it is sold in the app
choices.why: The commission is on digital goods used in the app.

choices.text: Double, because it is a service
choices.why: No such rate exists.

choices.text: It is forbidden to sell
choices.why: Selling outside services is allowed.

prompt: What is left of a price after the store's tax and commission is called the ___.
Why should a team open the store accounts before the app is finished?

choices.text: The fees go up after launch
choices.why: The fee is the same whenever you pay it.

choices.text: Apple reviews accounts in the order they open
choices.why: Review is of builds, not of accounts in a queue.

choices.text: Verification, D-U-N-S and a closed test take longer than the code
choices.why: Right. Count the calendar from the slowest step.

choices.text: An account cannot be opened without a finished app
choices.why: The reverse: the app needs the account.

prompt: Under the rule Google's help gave in 2025, at least how many testers must stay opted in to a new personal account's closed test?
The planner is ready, and its name is taken by another app in the App Store. When does the team find out?

choices.text: After launch, by a complaint
choices.why: The store refuses the duplicate before that.

prompt: The planner's Account Holder left the company, and nobody can sign in as them. What is the risk the team runs?

choices.text: The app is removed from the store at once
choices.why: Nothing happens at once; the risk is the next agreement or renewal.

choices.why: Their access stays; what they cannot do is sign.

choices.text: The distribution certificate is revoked
